title: Refuse a rebase or history rewrite of a lane branch from the batch runner or another lane
why: Runner 11 planned a "rebase of #1159" (q_max lane qmax-stale-rules-specs) on Nov 13; the coordinator stopped it at 11:05 CST. No guard would have: guard.py rule force-push passes a lease with --force-if-includes, and nothing refuses a local rebase of a lane branch. Harm: a rewrite on a lane's branch can drop the lane's commits or invalidate its review record (decision pr-review-record). SAMPLE 16:37 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 16:35): the #3421 lane squashed and force pushed its own PR branch before hand-in, a PR with records (record 6885181417 now at the new head). GUARD READ (hooks/guard.py, read in /root/claude-settings-main): rule force-push (lines 116-118, 4767-4772, id stale-safe-force-push) passes a lease with --force-if-includes, refuses --force or a `+` refspec, and asks a push that reaches the default branch. Nothing in that rule reads whether the PR holds a review record, and nothing refuses a local squash or rebase of a lane branch. Whether the #3421 push was a lease or bare is unknown (step lane-force-push-which-form, done, measured an earlier case). So a lease push on a PR with records would not have been stopped. This is the same gap this step names; no new step filed (one home). Kin: red-run-warn-before-commit (the cause on #3421 was a missing Red-run trailer).
source: coordinator 11:05 CST Nov 13; triage read of origin/main hooks/guard.py rule force-push
note: The guard refuses a rebase, reset or amend of a branch that is not the session's own lane branch, and a lease force-push to such a branch, in the batch runner's and lanes' sessions. Red case: the #1159 plan. Express (ruling drain-first-hold part 4: a fix that keeps work landing).
